about.title: Personal Injury Help in Colton, California
about.longDescription: Colton sits at a crossroads — literally. I-215 and I-10 cut through town, and Mt Vernon Avenue carries steady local traffic, all of which show up in the public collision counts each year: 452 injury collisions, 678 people hurt, and 14 lives lost in the most recent reporting year. Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m. tend to see more reported crashes, likely tied to end-of-week commute patterns. If you or someone you love was hurt in one of these incidents, sorting out medical bills, missed work, and insurance calls can feel like a full-time job on top of recovering physically. LawProactive is a free service — we are not a law firm — that connects injured people in Colton with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened and explain your options. There's no cost to talk to us, and the attorneys in our network only get paid if you recover compensation. You don't have to figure out the next step alone; reaching out costs you nothing and can help you understand where you stand.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: California's Two-Year Filing Window
items.desc: Most injury claims in California must be filed within two years of the incident, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can close the door on your case entirely.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be All-or-Nothing
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the crash. Your compensation is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages, such as pain and suffering, in typical injury cases. This can matter significantly if your injuries have affected your daily life.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover compensation for you. This removes the financial barrier to getting legal advice after a crash.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Colton?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of the incident to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity was involved, such as a city vehicle, the window can be as short as six months, so it's wise to act quickly.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the crash?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame. Your final award is simply reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Colton?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher volume on corridors like I-215, I-10, and Mt Vernon Avenue, with reports peaking on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m. These are neutral crash-count patterns, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney — we are not a law firm and don't charge you for the connection. Any attorney you work with operates on contingency, meaning they're only paid if you recover compensation.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In ordinary California injury cases, there's no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. The amount depends on the specifics of your case and injuries, which an attorney can help evaluate.
